main.title: Rhythm Heaven Megamix
main.subtitle: Nintendo SPD / TNX · Nintendo 3DS
main.summary: Rhythm Heaven Megamix is Nintendo and TNX's Nintendo 3DS collection of rhythm games. The player helps Tibby return home by completing scenes whose actions follow a musical pattern. Returning activities from the Game Boy Advance, DS and Wii games share the journey with new ones. A short instruction introduces each task, then the sound supplies the timing. The situations can involve unlikely creatures and everyday chores, but their common demand is simple: recognise when the next action belongs in the phrase and carry it out cleanly.

cards.heading: A journey built from small musical tasks
cards.text: Rhythm Heaven Megamix is Nintendo and TNX's Nintendo 3DS collection of rhythm games. The player helps Tibby return home by completing scenes whose actions follow a musical pattern. Returning activities from the Game Boy Advance, DS and Wii games share the journey with new ones. A short instruction introduces each task, then the sound supplies the timing. The situations can involve unlikely creatures and everyday chores, but their common demand is simple: recognise when the next action belongs in the phrase and carry it out cleanly.

cards.heading: Hear the gap between the beats
cards.text: Buttons provide the main controls, with an alternative touchscreen scheme also available. A timing display shows whether an input arrived early or late, giving a missed action more useful information than a failed score alone. Certain moments award a Skill Star for precise performance. The challenge lies in holding the pattern through rests, changes and interruptions. Once the gesture is familiar, the player has to trust the sound, resisting the urge to follow a distracting movement or answer before the music reaches its cue.

cards.heading: Several routines become one song
cards.text: Remix stages switch between learned activities within a shared musical sequence. Recognising the returning scene is only the beginning: its action must arrive in time even as another task replaces it. Challenge Train provides additional variations, including local multiplayer challenges and WarioWare-themed appearances. Strong performances earn currency for bonus games and collectibles. Megamix treats the earlier series as a repertoire worth playing again, then changes the combinations so that familiar gestures can still produce a fresh test of attention and timing.

main.title: Fire Emblem Fates
main.subtitle: Intelligent Systems · Nintendo 3DS
main.summary: Fire Emblem Fates is Intelligent Systems' tactical role-playing game for Nintendo 3DS. Corrin was born in Hoshido and raised by the royal family of Nohr. When the two kingdoms go to war, choosing a side means abandoning people who also consider Corrin their sibling. Birthright and Conquest follow those opposing allegiances, while Revelation offers a third route. The choice reaches beyond the story: each campaign provides different companions, maps and conditions for developing the army that must carry it through the conflict.

cards.heading: A family on either side of the border
cards.text: Fire Emblem Fates is Intelligent Systems' tactical role-playing game for Nintendo 3DS. Corrin was born in Hoshido and raised by the royal family of Nohr. When the two kingdoms go to war, choosing a side means abandoning people who also consider Corrin their sibling. Birthright and Conquest follow those opposing allegiances, while Revelation offers a third route. The choice reaches beyond the story: each campaign provides different companions, maps and conditions for developing the army that must carry it through the conflict.

cards.heading: One turn can decide the next battle
cards.text: Infantry, mounted units and flying fighters move across a grid, with terrain and weapon matchups shaping their chances. Adjacent allies can support an attack; pairing them instead provides protection and other advantages. Royal characters can use Dragon Veins to alter parts of a map, opening or closing routes at an important moment. A strong unit still needs a safe position when the enemy turn begins. The task is to arrange the whole army so that one successful attack does not leave its author surrounded.

cards.heading: Three campaigns with different demands
cards.text: Birthright allows opportunities to earn additional experience and money, while Conquest makes the supplies gained from its main battles particularly valuable. Revelation combines extra training opportunities with more elaborate battlefield devices. Between missions, My Castle provides shops and conversations that develop the group. Classic mode preserves the series' permanent deaths; Casual brings defeated allies back after battle. The versions let the same central dilemma support markedly different experiences, from a more forgiving introduction to a campaign that asks for careful use of a limited army.

main.title: Rocket League
main.subtitle: Rocket-powered cars turn football into an aerial sport
main.summary: Rocket League is a 2015 vehicular soccer video game developed and published by Psyonix.

cards.heading: Football with rocket-powered cars
cards.text: Rocket League is a 2015 vehicular soccer video game developed and published by Psyonix. A sequel to 2008's Supersonic Acrobatic Rocket-Powered Battle-Cars, Rocket League features up to eight players assigned to two teams, using "rocket-powered" vehicles to hit a ball into their opponent's goal and score points over the course of a match. The game includes single-player and multiplayer modes that can be played both locally and online, including cross-platform play between all versions.

cards.heading: From Battle-Cars to an evolving service
cards.text: Psyonix began formal development of Rocket League around 2013, refining the gameplay from Battle-Cars to address criticism and fan input. Psyonix also recognized their lack of marketing from Battle-Cars and engaged in both social media and promotions to market the game. Rocket League was first released on the PlayStation 4 and Windows respectively in July 2015, with ports for Xbox One and Nintendo Switch being released later on. Physical retail versions for PlayStation 4 and Xbox One were distributed starting in 2016 by 505 Games and later by Warner Bros. Interactive Entertainment. Versions for macOS and Linux were also released in 2016, but support for their online services was dropped in 2020. Rocket League is developed under the games as a service model; later updates for the game enabled the ability to modify core rules and added new game modes, including ones based on ice hockey, gridiron football and basketball. It has been offered as free-to-play since 2020, following Epic Games’ acquisition of Psyonix in 2019.

cards.heading: Players, awards and competition
cards.text: Rocket League was praised for its gameplay improvements over Supersonic Acrobatic Rocket Powered Battle-Cars, as well as its graphics and overall presentation, although some criticism was directed towards the game's physics engine. It has since been considered one of the greatest video games ever made. The game earned many industry awards and saw over 10 million sales and 40 million players by the beginning of 2018. Rocket League has also been adopted as an esport, with professional players participating through ESL and Major League Gaming along with Psyonix's own Rocket League Championship Series (RLCS).

main.title: The Great Ace Attorney: Adventures
main.subtitle: An ancestor takes the defence
main.summary: The Great Ace Attorney: Adventures is Capcom's courtroom adventure following Ryunosuke Naruhodo, an ancestor of Phoenix Wright, between Japan and Britain around the turn of the twentieth century. Accompanied by judicial assistant Susato Mikotoba, he encounters unfamiliar legal customs and the detective Herlock Sholmes. Its original Nintendo 3DS release begins a connected historical mystery that later reached a worldwide audience through The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles. Investigations and trials remain the foundation, but the setting gives the young defence lawyer new institutions and assumptions to understand.

cards.heading: An ancestor takes the defence
cards.text: The Great Ace Attorney: Adventures is Capcom's courtroom adventure following Ryunosuke Naruhodo, an ancestor of Phoenix Wright, between Japan and Britain around the turn of the twentieth century. Accompanied by judicial assistant Susato Mikotoba, he encounters unfamiliar legal customs and the detective Herlock Sholmes. Its original Nintendo 3DS release begins a connected historical mystery that later reached a worldwide audience through The Great Ace Attorney Chronicles. Investigations and trials remain the foundation, but the setting gives the young defence lawyer new institutions and assumptions to understand.

cards.heading: Correct the detective without losing the clue
cards.text: During a Dance of Deduction, Sholmes develops an impressive explanation from observations that do not quite support his conclusion. Ryunosuke examines the scene and redirects the deduction by identifying the overlooked detail. The pleasure comes from following a line of reasoning closely enough to recognise where it has gone astray. Objects and people can be inspected from different angles, making observation part of the correction. Sholmes supplies the performance and momentum, while the player supplies the small changes that turn it into a sounder account of events.

cards.heading: A jury must explain its verdict
cards.text: British trials introduce jurors whose opinions can bring a hearing close to an early conclusion. Summation Examination allows Ryunosuke to question those reasons and compare statements that conflict with one another. A contradiction between jurors can reopen the argument and provide another chance for the defence. Witnesses may also testify in groups, reacting to what the others say. The courtroom becomes a place where several accounts must be read together, extending the familiar search for contradictions beyond a single speaker and a single item of evidence.

main.title: Pokkén Tournament
main.subtitle: Pokémon fight at the player’s command
main.summary: Pokkén Tournament is Bandai Namco's action fighting game built around Pokémon, first released in Japanese arcades on 16 July 2015.

cards.heading: Pokémon fight at the player’s command
cards.text: Pokkén Tournament is Bandai Namco's action fighting game built around Pokémon, first released in Japanese arcades on 16 July 2015. Two players directly control individual creatures in battles that move between a free-roaming arena and a closer side-on confrontation. Familiar Pokémon attacks become actions to perform and time, giving the series' characters another kind of encounter. The player must read distance, an opponent's intentions and the opportunities attached to the current phase rather than issue commands to a larger party.

cards.heading: A change of phase changes the duel
cards.text: Field Phase allows movement around the arena, while Duel Phase concentrates the fighters into a more conventional head-to-head space. The shift changes which movements and attacks are useful. A Synergy Gauge builds towards stronger techniques and transformations, while Support Pokémon provide additional effects to help shape an exchange. The arcade machine uses a console-style controller rather than a traditional stick, reflecting the aim of making the fighting approachable. Its systems offer recognizable Pokémon powers inside a contest governed by immediate control and positioning.

cards.heading: An arcade idea reaches the living room
cards.text: The worldwide Wii U edition arrived on 18 March 2016, bringing the arcade design home with online competition and further content. A Shadow Mewtwo amiibo card accompanied early copies, and the expanded Pokkén Tournament DX followed on Switch in 2017. Producers Katsuhiro Harada and Masaaki Hoshino brought fighting-game experience to the collaboration, with Haruki Suzaki directing. The result gives each Pokémon a physical presence in the match, using changes of phase to connect an open arena encounter to the concentrated timing of a traditional fighting game.

main.title: Skyforge
main.subtitle: From immortal to god on the planet Aelion
main.summary: Skyforge is a discontinued free-to-play massively multiplayer online role-playing game developed by Allods Team in collaboration with Obsidian Entertainment, and published by My.com.

cards.heading: Immortals between science fiction and fantasy
cards.text: Skyforge is Allods Team and Obsidian Entertainment's free-to-play online role-playing game, first opened on Windows in July 2015. Players begin as immortals defending the planet Aelion and work towards becoming gods. Progression uses prestige drawn from a character's development, while allowing changes between classes. Greater power unlocks further equipment and activities; followers become another source of strength once the character reaches godhood. Its setting combines fantasy with alien invasions and advanced technology.

cards.heading: The closure of the PC and console versions
cards.text: On September 3, 2025, the Microsoft Windows versions were discontinued, while the console versions closed on October 29 in that same year.

main.title: N++
main.subtitle: From its PlayStation 4 debut to the expansions of Metanet’s platformer
main.summary: N++ is a platform video game developed and published by Metanet Software.

cards.heading: The third game in the N series
cards.text: N++ is Metanet Software's 2015 platform game, first released on PlayStation 4 as the third entry in the series begun by the Flash game N. Movement depends on momentum: speed and the angle of a surface affect a jump, while walls provide opportunities to rebound. Each level asks the player to reach an exit switch and then the doorway, avoiding hazards and collecting gold to extend the available time.

cards.heading: Expanding the platformer
cards.text: Five levels form an episode, giving the player successive courses to negotiate. A level editor and online sharing provide further challenges made by other players. The free Ultimate Edition update expanded the game in 2017, with additional levels, colour schemes and a Hardcore mode; a Switch edition followed in 2018. The tenth-anniversary TEN++ update in 2025 supplied more demanding Solo, Co-op and Race levels along with further palettes.

main.title: Fate/Grand Order
main.subtitle: Masters and Servants between turn-based battles and visual-novel storytelling
main.summary: Fate/Grand Order is a free-to-play mobile RPG based on Type-Moon?s Fate franchise, combining turn-based battles with visual-novel storytelling.

cards.heading: A mobile game in the world of Fate
cards.text: Fate/Grand Order is a free-to-play Japanese gacha mobile game, developed by Lasengle (formerly Delightworks) using Unity, and published by Aniplex, a subsidiary of Sony Music Entertainment Japan. The game is based on Type-Moon's Fate/stay night franchise, and was released in Japan on 30 July 2015 for Android, and on 12 August 2015, for iOS. English-language versions followed on 25 June 2017 in the United States and Canada, and a Korean version was released on 21 November 2017. An arcade version titled Fate/Grand Order Arcade was released by Sega in Japan on 26 July 2018.

cards.heading: Masters, Servants and turn-based combat
cards.text: The game is centered around turn-based combat where the player, who takes on the role of a "Master", summons and commands powerful familiars known as "Servants" to battle enemies. The story narrative is presented in a visual novel format, and each Servant has their own scenario which the player can explore. Servants are obtained through the gacha mechanic. As of July 2021, the game grossed $5.4 billion worldwide, making it the seventh highest-grossing mobile game of all time. Total revenues reached $7 billion by September 2023.

main.title: Until Dawn
main.subtitle: Decisions and performances shape a night of survival
main.summary: Until Dawn is a 2015 interactive drama survival horror game developed by Supermassive Games and published by Sony Computer Entertainment.

cards.heading: Eight friends, branching outcomes
cards.text: Until Dawn is a 2015 interactive drama survival horror game developed by Supermassive Games and published by Sony Computer Entertainment. Players assume control of eight young adults who have to survive on Blackwood Mountain when their lives are threatened. The game features a butterfly effect system in which players must make choices that may change the story. All major playable characters can survive or die, depending on the choices made. Players explore the environment from a third-person perspective and find clues that may help solve the mystery.

cards.heading: From PlayStation Move to performance capture
cards.text: Until Dawn was originally planned as a first-person game for the PlayStation 3's motion controller PlayStation Move. The motion controls were dropped when it became a PlayStation 4 game. The script was written by Larry Fessenden and Graham Reznick, who sought to create the video game equivalent of a slasher film. The development team took inspiration from various sources. These include the movies Evil Dead II and Poltergeist, and video games Heavy Rain, Resident Evil, and Silent Hill. To ensure the game was scary, the team used a galvanic skin response test to measure playtesters' fear levels when playing it. Jason Graves composed the soundtrack and Guerrilla Games' Decima game engine was used for the graphics. Several noted actors, including Rami Malek, Hayden Panettiere, Meaghan Martin, Brett Dalton, Jordan Fisher, Nichole Sakura, and Peter Stormare provided motion capture and voice acting.

cards.heading: A PS4 horror story and its later adaptations
cards.text: Until Dawn reached PlayStation 4 in August 2015 and exceeded Sony's sales expectations. Reviewers praised its branching outcomes, characters and quick-time events, while criticising the controls. Supermassive followed it with Rush of Blood and The Inpatient, then returned to a similar form of horror with The Quarry in 2022. A PlayStation 5 and Windows remake appeared in October 2024, and a film adaptation followed in April 2025.

main.title: Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain
main.subtitle: Venom Snake and the aftermath of Ground Zeroes
main.summary: Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain is a 2015 action-adventure stealth game developed and published by Konami.

cards.heading: Venom Snake follows Ground Zeroes
cards.text: Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain is Konami's 2015 stealth action adventure, directed by Hideo Kojima as a continuation of Ground Zeroes. In 1984, mercenary leader Venom Snake travels through Soviet-occupied Afghanistan and the Angola–Zaire border region, seeking revenge on those who destroyed his forces. Missions take place in large open areas, with reconnaissance, equipment and companions giving the player different ways to approach an objective.

cards.heading: Stealth, companions and an expanding base
cards.text: The game is played from a third-person perspective in an open world which can be explored either on foot or by modes of transport. Snake can use a wide repertoire of weapons and items, and receive assistance from several AI companions, allowing the player to combat enemies either stealthily or directly. Enemy soldiers and resources found in the world can be transported to Snake's headquarters, allowing for its expansion and the development of further technology. The game includes two separate multiplayer modes, Metal Gear Online (also known as Metal Gear Online 3) and Forward Operating Bases (FOBs); the latter mode allows players to develop FOBs, which can then be invaded by other players.

cards.heading: Reception and the Definitive Experience
cards.text: The September 2015 release received praise for its infiltration systems, open areas and performances. Its repeated missions and ending drew criticism, and the narrative divided reviewers. Konami reported six million units shipped by December. The 2016 Definitive Experience subsequently brought The Phantom Pain together with Ground Zeroes and their additional content, placing the prologue and main game in one package.

cards.heading: Weather and the time of an approach
cards.text: The day-night cycle and changing weather affect how a location can be approached. A base seen clearly from a distant hill may offer a different route after dark or during a storm. Vehicles and companions add further options to the equipment selected before departure. The player can prepare a plan around those conditions, then adapt it as the mission changes.

cards.heading: Reconnaissance before an infiltration
cards.text: Reconnaissance turns an open area into a set of possible routes. Binoculars and markers help the player study guards and choose an entry point, while distance, visibility and noise influence the approach. An alarm may force a change of plan. The same location can therefore support another attempt with different equipment, timing or movement through the base.

cards.heading: Recovering resources for Mother Base
cards.text: Fulton extraction connects a mission to Mother Base. Recovering soldiers, vehicles and containers adds staff or resources to the organisation, supporting its expansion and the development of technology. A useful recruit can give the player a reason to take another risk after the main objective has been met. What returns from the field changes the options available for later sorties.

cards.heading: Briefings, tapes and the story between missions
cards.text: Briefings, audio tapes, missions and details at Mother Base carry different parts of the story. The player encounters that material alongside the open-world operations, choosing when to listen or examine the base between assignments. This distribution places some of the narrative within the same intervals used for planning and development. The approach also contributed to the debate around the game's storytelling and ending.
